description: This lab targets a Server-Side Template Injection vulnerability in Yeti 2.1.11's export feature. By injecting malicious Jinja2 expressions into a custom export template, attackers gain remote code execution. The exploit enables enumeration of sensitive files and SSH key injection, leading to persistent root access on the host.

name: CVE-2024-46986_Attack
description: This lab targets CVE-2024-46986 in CamaleonCMS v2.8.0, where default credentials and an insecure file upload mechanism allow command injection via Ruby scripts. Attackers can upload malicious scripts into application initializers, enabling either remote shell access or direct command execution, culminating in full system compromise as root.

name: CVE-2024-48061
description: In this lab, we will exploit the CVE-2024-48061 vulnerability in LangFlow to gain remote code execution. By injecting a malicious payload into the LangFlow interface, we can execute arbitrary commands on the system, leading to root access. This lab focuses on exploiting remote code execution vulnerabilities in web applications.

name: CVE-2024-48573
description: This lab explores CVE-2024-48573 in AquilaCMS, where a NoSQL injection vulnerability in the password reset API enables account takeover. Combined with a plugin upload feature, attackers escalate to remote code execution by deploying and deactivating a crafted Node.js plugin. The exploit chain results in a reverse shell as root.

name: CVE-2024-48914_Attack
description: A Vendure e-commerce platform exposes an unauthenticated file read vulnerability through improper path validation in its asset server. Identified as CVE-2024-48914, this flaw allows attackers to access sensitive system files, such as private SSH keys, ultimately leading to root access via SSH login on affected systems.

name: CVE-2024-51482
description: In this lab, we will exploit the CVE-2024-51482 vulnerability in ZoneMinder to gain unauthorized access to the system. By leveraging a SQL injection vulnerability, we can dump the `Users` table from the database, crack the password hash for the root user, and gain root access via SSH. This lab focuses on exploiting SQL injection vulnerabilities and password cracking techniques.

name: CVE-2024-5334
description: This challenge targets a vulnerable AI service exposing arbitrary file read vulnerabilities (CVE-2024-40422 and CVE-2024-5334). Learners exploit these flaws to retrieve sensitive files, including SSH keys, leading to root access. Mastering enumeration, crafting precise payloads, and understanding service misconfigurations are essential to achieving full system compromise.

name: CVE-2024-55415
description: A vulnerable Laravel application running Voyager v1.7.0 is exposed to an authenticated arbitrary file read vulnerability (CVE-2024-55415). Attackers who access the admin panel with default credentials can manipulate download queries to retrieve sensitive files such as private SSH keys. Successful exploitation leads to full root access via SSH login, highlighting the dangers of misconfigured access controls.

name: CVE-2024-55963
description: This lab demonstrates an unauthenticated Remote Code Execution vulnerability (CVE-2024-55963) in Appsmith versions before v1.52. By exploiting PostgreSQL’s COPY FROM PROGRAM feature, attackers can execute arbitrary shell commands on the host system. Learners will compromise the backend database through Appsmith’s misconfigured plugin integrations and exfiltrate sensitive files directly from the server.

name: CVE-2024-56145
description: This challenge focuses on exploiting a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in Craft CMS (CVE-2024-56145). By leveraging an exposed vector in certain PHP configurations, attackers can execute arbitrary commands on the server.

name: CVE-2025-10952
description: This lab showcases an arbitrary file read vulnerability in ml-logger, where improper validation of the key argument in the stream_handler function enables attackers to traverse directories and exfiltrate sensitive files. By chaining the /glob and /stream endpoints, an attacker can enumerate and extract critical files like private SSH keys, leading to unauthorized remote access and full system compromise as root.

name: CVE-2025-21624
description: This lab challenges participants to exploit an authenticated file upload vulnerability (CVE-2025-21624) in ClipBucket V5.5.1’s Manage Playlist feature to achieve remote code execution. By uploading a PHP web shell, attackers gain system access and escalate privileges to root using unrestricted sudo access.

name: CVE-2025-27136
description: This lab challenges you to exploit an XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability in Local-S3, a self-hosted S3-compatible storage service. By leveraging this flaw, you can extract sensitive files from the system, including SSH private keys, and gain unauthorized access via SSH. This scenario tests your ability to perform enumeration, exploit misconfigured XML parsers, and establish remote access through stolen credentials.

name: CVE-2025-27520
description: A critical insecure deserialization vulnerability in BentoML 1.4.2 (CVE-2025-27520) enables unauthenticated attackers to achieve Remote Code Execution. Exploiting the vulnerable serde.py module, an attacker crafts a malicious pickle payload to execute arbitrary commands, leading to complete system compromise. This lab emphasizes the risks of insecure serialization in machine learning frameworks and the importance of safe deserialization practices.

name: CVE-2025-27636
description: Target a web application powered by Apache Camel v4.10 vulnerable to CVE-2025-27636—a header filter bypass flaw. Manipulate HTTP headers to inject commands into a misconfigured endpoint that executes system commands as root. Chain the vulnerability with remote file retrieval and achieve a reverse shell without requiring privilege escalation steps.

name: CVE-2025-2945_attack
description: This lab explores CVE-2025-2945, an authenticated remote code execution vulnerability in pgAdmin 4. Attackers begin by enumerating exposed services, brute-forcing database credentials, and discovering valid web UI accounts. After gaining authenticated access, the vulnerable query tool is abused to execute arbitrary commands on the server, leading to shell access and system compromise.

name: CVE-2025-30208
description: A misconfigured Vite server exposes a critical file read vulnerability (CVE-2025-30208), enabling attackers to bypass path restrictions via crafted query parameters. By exploiting this flaw, an attacker can access sensitive files like SSH keys and escalate to root access. This challenge highlights the risks of improper input validation and insecure default settings in web development frameworks.

name: CVE-2025-31131
description: A Path Traversal vulnerability in YesWiki (CVE-2025-31131) allows unauthenticated attackers to access sensitive server files by exploiting the squelette parameter. Improper input validation enables directory traversal sequences, exposing critical data such as private SSH keys. This vulnerability can lead to full system compromise when leveraged effectively.

name: CVE-2025-32101_Attack
description: This lab focuses on exploiting CVE-2025-32101, a PHP Object Injection vulnerability in UNA CMS version ≤14.0.0-RC4. By abusing insecure deserialization through the profile_id parameter in BxBaseMenuSetAclLevel.php, unauthenticated attackers can gain remote code execution. The lab culminates in a reverse shell as the web server user, simulating a real-world initial compromise vector via a misconfigured CMS.

name: CVE-2025-32375
description: This challenge centers on CVE-2025-32375, a critical RCE vulnerability in BentoML versions prior to 1.4.8 caused by insecure deserialization. Learners must exploit the runner server's mishandling of serialized data to execute arbitrary commands and gain root access via a crafted pickle payload in a malicious POST request.

name: CVE-2025-32463
description: This lab explores local privilege escalation by exploiting a vulnerability in Sudo (CVE-2025-32463). Learners begin with access to a restricted shell and leverage a flawed chroot mechanism that mishandles nsswitch.conf loading. By crafting a malicious shared library and manipulating Sudo’s root directory, attackers can escalate privileges to root and access protected data.

name: CVE-2025-50817
description: This lab explores multiple web application flaws leading to full system compromise. Learners begin with a path traversal vulnerability to extract sensitive files, escalate to authenticated access via Flask session tampering, and exploit a LaTeX injection to gain a reverse shell. The final privilege escalation leverages CVE-2025-50817, an import flaw in the Python future module, to hijack root-level cron execution.

name: CVE-2025-50946
description: Target a misconfigured OliveTin instance (version 2025.4.22) exposed on a non-standard port and exploit a command injection vulnerability in its theme installation feature. By injecting OS commands through the “Theme’s Git Repository” field, gain remote code execution and escalate directly to a root shell via a crafted reverse shell payload. This challenge reinforces techniques in identifying service versions, exploiting web-based command injection, crafting reverse shell payloads, and leveraging misconfigurations in web interfaces for privilege escalation.

name: CVE-2025-5880_Attack
description: A misconfigured instance of the Whistle Web Debugging Proxy exposes a vulnerable endpoint, allowing unauthenticated attackers to exploit CVE-2025-5880. Through path traversal, sensitive system files are retrievable, including private SSH keys. This ultimately leads to full system compromise with root access via SSH.

name: CVE-2026-22200
description: This lab explores CVE-2026-22200, a PDF file-read vulnerability affecting osTicket 1.18.2 and earlier through the mPDF library. Learners will enumerate the target, identify the vulnerable application, exploit malicious PDF rendering to disclose sensitive server files, recover SSH credentials, and leverage the exposed private key to obtain root access.

name: Dawn2
description: Utilize enumeration and web enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Engage in binary exploitation and buffer overflow techniques to enhance your skills. This lab is designed to capitalize on your abilities in vulnerability exploitation.

name: Dawn3
description: Employ enumeration and FTP enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Engage in binary exploitation and buffer overflow methods to enhance your skills. This lab is designed to capitalize on your abilities in vulnerability exploitation.

name: DC5
description: Utilize enumeration and web enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Leverage exploitation of the LFI vulnerability and engage in log poisoning. Implement privilege escalation strategies and harness the exploitation of GNU Screen. Additionally, abuse sudo permissions to enhance your access. This lab is designed to capitalize on your skills in vulnerability exploitation.

name: Deception
description: Engage in enumeration, web enumeration, and WordPress enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Implement privilege escalation strategies and harness the abuse of sudo permissions to enhance your access. This lab is designed to capitalize on your skills in vulnerability exploitation.

name: Deployer
description: In this lab, we'll leverage PHP deserialization and local file inclusion vulnerabilities to compromise this target by executing a reverse shell uploaded via FTP. We'll then employ Docker to build a new image to exfiltrate the root SSH key for elevated access.

name: Depreciated
description: By abusing GraphQL and a Python messaging service, access will be gained to the target system, allowing for escalation to root privileges. This lab focuses on exploiting API vulnerabilities and privilege escalation techniques.

name: DepthB2R
description: Employ enumeration and web enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Engage in privilege escalation strategies and harness the abuse of sudo permissions to enhance your access. This lab is designed to capitalize on your skills in vulnerability exploitation.

name: Detection
description: You will leverage enumeration techniques to uncover potential vulnerabilities. The lab involves exploiting CVE-2024-32651 to demonstrate its impact on system security. This lab focuses on understanding and exploiting vulnerabilities to enhance security awareness.

name: dev_working
description: This challenge involves enumerating an Apache Solr instance to extract credentials, leveraging them for MySQL database access, and cracking password hashes to gain an initial foothold. Once inside, privilege escalation is achieved by exploiting a SUID binary that dynamically loads a shared library, allowing for root shell execution.

name: DevArmor
description: DevArmor presents a multi‑stage compromise of an internal environment. Attackers enumerate a vault subdomain running FortiLock, abuse a hidden registration API, and exploit an IDOR flaw to harvest other users’ credentials. Gaining access to an internal Gogs instance reveals command execution through a known exploit, leading to host access. Privilege escalation is achieved by abusing a misconfigured backup manager and the vulnerable unzip‑stream package (CVE‑2024‑42471) to overwrite sensitive files and gain root control.

name: Develop
description: This lab focuses on exploiting a PHP web application vulnerable to type juggling, enabling authentication bypass using *magic hashes*. Learners will uncover sensitive files through blind Local File Inclusion (LFI), escalate privileges by exploiting Docker group misconfigurations, and gain root access through container manipulation.

name: Devnal
description: This lab explores a misconfigured custom kernel module that provides arbitrary read and write access to kernel memory.

name: Dibble
description: To breach this lab, you'll start by discovering an application running NodeJS and gain a foothold by registering a user. You'll then elevate your privileges by altering a cookie value. This lab teaches you about user registration, privilege escalation through cookie manipulation, code injection, and leveraging SUID for root access.

name: DocsGPT
description: This lab focuses on exploiting CVE-2025-0868, a critical command injection flaw in DocsGPT. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary Python code through the /api/remote endpoint due to unsafe use of eval() on JSON data. Learners must identify the vulnerability, craft an exploit, gain root access, and retrieve the proof.

name: Driftwood
description: A Linux host running SSH and a web server with a content management system powering a surf club site, plus a custom staff console binary for local privilege escalation.

name: DVR4
description: A foothold on the target system will be established by exploiting a directory traversal vulnerability in the DVR software to access an SSH key. Privileges will then be elevated by decoding the Administrator password found in a configuration file. This lab focuses on exploiting vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Educated
description: Enumeration techniques are leveraged to identify potential vulnerabilities, including web enumeration. The lab focuses on exploiting SQL vulnerabilities, practicing privilege escalation, and performing buffer overflow or binary exploitation. This lab emphasizes understanding and exploiting vulnerabilities to enhance security awareness.

name: Emporium
description: Source code analysis of a PHP website vulnerable to insecure deserialization will be performed to establish an initial foothold. Privileges will then be escalated by exploiting a Zip Path Traversal vulnerability in PclZip, allowing a PHP reverse shell to be uploaded for root access. This lab focuses on exploiting application vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: ERP
description: A blind SQL injection will be leveraged to discover an ERP system vulnerable to arbitrary file upload, establishing an initial foothold. Privileges will then be escalated by accessing a system not available to external users to obtain root access. This lab focuses on exploiting database vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Escape
description: To compromise this lab, you will leverage a file upload vulnerability in a WordPress application to gain an initial foothold. You'll then escalate by escaping a Docker container and exploiting a misconfiguration in the capabilities of the OpenSSL binary, enhancing your skills in container escapes and misconfigured binary exploitation.

name: Exfiltrated
description: In this lab, we will exploit the target through an authenticated file upload bypass vulnerability in Subrion CMS that leads to remote code execution. We will then exploit a root cron job via a script running exiftool every minute.

name: Exghost
description: In this lab, FTP will be brute-forced using default credentials, and a pcap file will be analyzed, leading to remote code execution in the exif tool. Privilege escalation will then be achieved by exploiting a vulnerable version of the policykit-1 package. This lab focuses on brute-force techniques and privilege escalation methods.

name: Extplorer
description: This lab demonstrates exploiting a file upload vulnerability in eXtplorer to achieve remote code execution by uploading a PHP web shell. After initial compromise as www-data, learners escalate privileges by exploiting the disk group membership of user dora, using debugfs to access sensitive system files (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow), cracking the root password hash with john, and obtaining root access.

name: Fail
description: To compromise this lab, you will exploit an open rsync share then escalate privileges by exploiting misconfigured service and file permissions in the fail2ban security software. This lab enhances your understanding of file-sharing vulnerabilities and privilege escalation through service misconfigurations.

name: Fanatastic
description: This lab will be exploited by leveraging vulnerabilities identified in Grafana v8.3.0. Publicly available exploits will be used to obtain a secret key, which will then be decrypted to retrieve the system admin password, allowing for root-level access to the system. This lab focuses on exploiting application vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Fikklish
description: A vulnerability in Weblate 4.11 will be exploited to establish an initial foothold. Privilege escalation will be performed by thoroughly enumerating the lab to discover a set of credentials and exploiting an argument injection in Git v1.10.2. This lab focuses on exploiting vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: filebrowser
description: Gain access through a misconfigured FileBrowser instance exposed on port 8080, where default credentials grant admin privileges. The lab challenges you to manipulate user settings to execute system commands, escalate privileges via SSH key injection, and exploit a SUID binary (aa-exec) to achieve root access.

name: Fired
description: In this lab, you will leverage enumeration techniques to identify potential vulnerabilities. The lab involves exploiting CVE-2023-32315 and practicing privilege escalation to gain unauthorized access. This lab focuses on understanding and exploiting vulnerabilities to enhance security awareness.

name: Fish
description: In this lab, we will leverage a directory traversal vulnerability in Oracle GlassFish and exploit a credential disclosure in SynaMan to gain a foothold on the target system. We will then elevate our access by abusing the installed antivirus, TotalAV. This lab focuses on exploiting web application vulnerabilities and privilege escalation techniques.

name: Five86.2
description: Employ enumeration and WordPress enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Utilize brute force attacks and engage in privilege escalation. Additionally, harness sudo permission abuse to enhance your access. This lab is designed to capitalize on your skills in vulnerability exploitation.

name: Flasky
description: In this lab, you will exploit the target by obtaining and modifying the JWT cookie for a Flask web application, successfully bypassing the app's authentication controls. You will then retrieve and crack an encrypted Cisco password for a user found in a config file, enabling you to SSH into the target.

name: Flimsy
description: This lab demonstrates exploiting a Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in Apache APISIX 2.8 (CVE-2022-24112) to bypass IP restrictions and achieve a reverse shell as the franklin user. Privilege escalation is performed by leveraging a writable apt configuration directory to inject a reverse shell payload into the cron-executed apt-get update command. This lab emphasizes API exploitation, cronjob abuse, and misconfigured package management for root access.

name: flink
description: This lab explores how an exposed Apache Flink dashboard can be abused to achieve remote code execution by uploading a malicious JAR file. Once initial access is gained, learners pivot to root by exploiting sudo privileges allowing execution of the Flink binary. This misconfiguration enables escalation via another crafted JAR payload, demonstrating the risks of unsecured interfaces and mismanaged permissions.

name: flow
description: Approaches for identifying potential vulnerabilities are utilized in this lab. The focus is on exploiting CVE-2024-1483, practicing privilege escalation, and abusing SUDO permissions for unauthorized access. This lab emphasizes understanding and exploiting vulnerabilities to enhance security awareness.

name: Flower
description: An arbitrary file upload vulnerability in TinyFileManager 2.4.3 will be leveraged to gain initial access. A SUID binary will then be reversed, and a buffer overflow exploited to obtain root access. This lab focuses on file upload vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Flu
description: You are required to leverage enumeration techniques, including web enumeration, to uncover potential vulnerabilities. The lab involves exploiting CVE-2022-26134 and abusing cronjobs to gain unauthorized access. This lab focuses on understanding and exploiting vulnerabilities to enhance security awareness.

name: Forward
description: We'll decrypt a password found in an SMB share to access a user's home directory. After gaining access, we'll place a malicious file and trigger it by sending an email to the user to obtain a shell. Finally, we'll exploit the SUID permissions on dosbox to overwrite the passwd file, granting us root access.

name: Fowsniff
description: Utilize enumeration and web enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Engage in password cracking and apply mail server enumeration methods. Additionally, implement privilege escalation strategies and leverage kernel exploitation techniques to enhance your access. This lab is designed to capitalize on your skills in vulnerability exploitation.

name: Fractal
description: The combination of the _fragment URL and the secret on the Symfony Profiler will be utilized to obtain an initial foothold. Once on the lab, thorough enumeration will be conducted, followed by uploading a user-generated set of authorized keys to gain root access via SSH. This lab focuses on exploiting web application vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Fuxa
description: Fuxa, a SCADA/HMI dashboard software, is vulnerable to remote code execution through its script execution feature. Attackers can create and execute JavaScript payloads directly on the server, allowing them to gain a reverse shell and escalate to root access.

name: G00g
description: In this lab, you will exploit the target by guessing the default web application credentials and bypassing two-factor authentication using a default secret key. This will enable you to exploit a local file inclusion vulnerability. This lab teaches you how to identify and exploit common web application vulnerabilities, emphasizing the importance of securing sensitive information.

name: GetSetGo
description: GetSetGo is a Linux machine hosting a Java web application server. Work from web enumeration to a foothold, recover credentials, deploy a payload, then escalate to root.

name: Glider
description: An XML External Entity attack will be exploited in a web application, followed by source code analysis of a PHP file to discover command execution in the preg_replace() function. To escalate privileges, a Man-in-the-Middle attack against an MQTT server will be performed to discover credentials that grant root access. This lab focuses on exploiting injection vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: GLPI
description: CVE-2022-35914 will be exploited to target GLPI 10.0.2 for initial access. Once on the box, a vulnerable Jetty Server will be exploited to gain root access. This lab focuses on exploiting known vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: GourmetDelight
description: This lab focuses on exploiting a vulnerable web application and containerized environment through chained vulnerabilities. Learners identify a time-based blind SQL injection to harvest credentials, reuse them on a separate login portal, and exploit command injection to gain a reverse shell in a Docker container. A leaked email exposes SSH credentials, granting host access. Privilege escalation is performed via a cron-executed Python script vulnerable to library hijacking.

name: Gradle
description: A serialization vulnerability in Apache OFBiz will be exploited to establish an initial foothold. Privileges will be escalated by exploiting a command injection vulnerability in a Gradle task to gain root access. This lab focuses on exploiting serialization vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Graph
description: In this lab, an exposed GraphQL instance will be exploited using SQL injection to retrieve a password and gain a foothold. Subsequently, a newline injection vulnerability in a custom program will be exploited to achieve root access. This lab focuses on exploiting application vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Groove
description: You are required to leverage enumeration techniques, including web enumeration, to identify potential vulnerabilities. The lab involves exploiting SQL injection vulnerabilities and performing password cracking to gain unauthorized access. This lab focuses on understanding and exploiting vulnerabilities to enhance security awareness.

name: GRPC
description: An attacker exploits an improperly secured GRPC service to read internal files and uncover an exposed remote command execution function. By calling an undocumented GRPC method with a hardcoded authentication key, they execute arbitrary commands, establish a reverse shell, and escalate privileges by abusing a misconfigured Kapacitor instance. This lab highlights GRPC security flaws, unauthorized API access, command execution, and privilege escalation techniques.

name: Hallucination
description: An arbitrary file read vulnerability in a Minecraft server will be exploited before uploading a malicious .jar file to establish an initial foothold. Root access will then be obtained by modifying a vulnerable SUID binary. This lab focuses on exploiting file read vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Hasura
description:
This lab challenges you to enumerate and exploit a Hasura-based web application. By registering a user and escalating privileges, you gain admin access, uncover a PostgreSQL injection vulnerability, and extract plaintext credentials. Leveraging database command execution, you escalate to the postgres user and ultimately gain full system control as root.

**The blind SQLi may take longer than 5-10mins to fully exploit**

name: Hawat
description: In this lab, you will discover the source code for an application, and by analyzing it, you will identify an SQL injection vulnerability that can be exploited to gain remote code execution on the machine, ultimately leading to a root shell, employing techniques to recognize and exploit SQL injection vulnerabilities to escalate privileges effectively.

name: HAWordy
description: In this lab, the machine is exploited through a vulnerability in a web application, leading to unauthorized actions. Initial escalation is achieved by exploiting misconfigured permissions on a binary, which allows the attacker to modify system files and introduce a new root user.

name: Heist
description: In this lab, we will leverage a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability to retrieve an NTLMv2 handshake via responder. We will then exploit the privileges of two users to gain write permissions on the C:Windowssystem32utilman.exe binary and trigger system-integrity execution through RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol). This lab focuses on privilege escalation techniques and bypassing system integrity protections.

name: Hepet
description: In this lab, you will exploit the target by uncovering important information in emails accessed through leaked credentials. You will utilize this information to send a spreadsheet containing a malicious macro, granting you a low-privileged shell. Finally, you will escalate your privileges by exploiting a misconfigured service.

name: Hetemit
description: To exploit this lab, you will target a custom API endpoint and a dangerous Python module, followed by privilege escalation through write permissions on a service file. This lab enhances your skills in API exploitation and misconfiguration abuse for privilege escalation.

name: Hub
description: This lab focuses on enumeration techniques, particularly web enumeration, to identify potential vulnerabilities. It also covers exploiting a malicious file upload vulnerability to gain initial access. Learners will learn the practical implications of these methods in real-world scenarios.

name: Hunit
description: To exploit this lab, you will enumerate a web application to discover an API endpoint that leaks user information, providing SSH access as a low-privileged user. Finally, you'll escalate your privileges by cloning the repository to your attack lab and injecting a malicious payload using the git account. This lab will improve your skills in information gathering, SSH access exploitation, and privilege escalation through version control systems.

name: Hutch
description: To exploit this lab, you will enumerate LDAP and utilize the IIS web server with WebDAV enabled to gain code execution then escalate privileges by leveraging Microsoft LAPS, ultimately discovering the random password for the Administrator user through LDAP. This lab will enhance your skills in exploiting LDAP vulnerabilities, utilizing WebDAV for file uploads, and understanding Microsoft LAPS for privilege escalation.

name: Illusion
description: In this lab, PHP Type Juggling will be exploited to bypass a login page, followed by Server Side Template Injection to achieve initial code execution. Privilege escalation will then be accomplished by exploiting Redis memory space. This lab focuses on exploiting application vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: image
description: The lab focuses on various enumeration techniques, including web enumeration, to identify vulnerabilities in applications. It teaches Learners to exploit an ImageMagick vulnerability for initial access. Finally, the lab covers how to abuse SUID binaries for privilege escalation.

name: Infilo
description: This lab challenges you to exploit prototype pollution vulnerabilities in a Node.js web application. By manipulating deeply merged user input, you’ll escalate privileges to admin and enable hidden features such as the file explorer. Ultimately, this leads to remote access via stolen SSH keys from exposed server directories.

name: Injecto
description: A foothold on the target system will be established by exploiting a local file inclusion vulnerability in conjunction with a PHP deserialization vulnerability. We will then elevate access to root by leveraging curl with SUID. This lab focuses on exploiting file inclusion and deserialization vulnerabilities, as well as privilege escalation techniques.

name: Interface
description: To breach this lab, you'll brute-force user credentials in a NodeJS web application to gain an initial foothold. Subsequently, you'll exploit an OS command injection vulnerability in the application to obtain a root shell. This lab enhances your skills in credential brute-forcing and exploiting command injection vulnerabilities for privilege escalation.

name: Internal
description: In this lab, exploit a vulnerability in an outdated version of the Microsoft Windows SMB server (CVE-2009-3103), discovered through a fingerprinting scan of network services. This exercise enhances your skills in vulnerability detection and exploiting network service weaknesses.

name: InvokeAI_RCE
description: An attacker exploits a remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2024-12029) in InvokeAI by abusing the /api/v2/models/install endpoint. By crafting a malicious pickle payload, they inject a public SSH key into the root user's authorized keys, enabling SSH access. This lab demonstrates deserialization attacks, remote execution, and persistence techniques via key injection.

name: IronSpire
description: IronSpire is a hard Linux machine hosting a web application and SSH. Chain web enumeration into a foothold, then work through layered privilege escalation to root.

name: Jacko
description: To compromise this lab, you will discover a misconfigured H2 database with default credentials. You will exploit this misconfiguration to gain command execution. Finally, you will escalate privileges by leveraging a DLL hijacking vulnerability in Fujitsu's Paperstream IP program, enhancing your skills in vulnerability detection and privilege escalation techniques.

name: JISCTF
description: Employ enumeration and web enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Leverage the exploitation of file upload vulnerabilities and engage in log poisoning. Additionally, implement privilege escalation strategies to enhance your access. This lab is designed to capitalize on your skills in vulnerability exploitation.

name: Jordak
description: Approaches for identifying potential vulnerabilities are utilized in this lab. The focus is on exploiting CVE-2023-26469, practicing privilege escalation, and abusing SUDO permissions for unauthorized access. This lab emphasizes understanding and exploiting vulnerabilities to enhance security awareness.

name: Keights
description: Enumeration techniques are leveraged to identify potential vulnerabilities in Kubernetes. The lab involves enumerating Kubernetes components to uncover security weaknesses. This lab focuses on understanding and exploiting vulnerabilities to enhance security awareness.

name: Kevin
description: Engage in leveraging default credentials and a public exploit against HP Power Manager. This process will include successfully exploiting the application using a public Metasploit module. This activity enhances your skills in exploiting vulnerabilities and utilizing available tools for effective system access.

name: KeyVault
description: This lab demonstrates exploiting a PHP HMAC bypass vulnerability to retrieve sensitive credentials and gain initial access via SSH. Learners will escalate privileges by reverse engineering a PyInstaller-packed binary, extracting a base64-encoded root password, and using it to achieve full system access. The lab highlights web application vulnerabilities, binary analysis, and privilege escalation through custom script exploitation.

name: Kyoto
description: This lab covers various enumeration techniques, including SMB enumeration, to identify potential vulnerabilities within the target system. Learners will engage in binary exploitation, specifically focusing on buffer overflow attacks, to gain initial access. Additionally, exploiting Group Policy Objects (GPOs) will provide further opportunities for privilege escalation. This lab teaches the significance of thorough enumeration and exploitation methods in penetration testing.

name: LaVita
description: The lab will leverage enumeration techniques, including web enumeration, to uncover potential vulnerabilities. You will also exploit CVE-2021-3129 and demonstrate how to abuse SUDO permissions for unauthorized access. This lab focuses on understanding and exploiting vulnerabilities to enhance security awareness.

name: law
description: The lab emphasizes enumeration techniques, including web enumeration, to uncover vulnerabilities in applications. Learners will exploit CVE-2022-35914 to gain initial access. Additionally, the lab teaches how to abuse cronjobs for privilege escalation.

name: LazySysAdmin
description: Employ enumeration and web enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Engage in privilege escalation strategies to enhance your access. This lab is designed to capitalize on your skills in vulnerability exploitation.

name: Leaked
description: A minimal HTTP service exposes endpoints with varied access restrictions, one of which filters based on an unknown API key. By exploiting a server-side URL fetching feature and bypassing Same-Origin Policy via XS-Leaks, an attacker can brute-force the numeric API key and gain unauthorized access to sensitive functionality restricted to localhost.

name: Levram
description: In this lab, we will conduct web enumeration to identify vulnerabilities, specifically focusing on exploiting CVE-2021-32849 and CVE-2021-43857. Following the exploitation, we will escalate privileges to gain higher access on the system. This lab teaches techniques for identifying and exploiting specific vulnerabilities, as well as methods for privilege escalation.

name: Leyla
description: The Leyla lab explores the exploitation of a vulnerable web application featuring Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) and a WordPress plugin flaw (CVE-2024-8352).

name: Lunar
description: In this lab, source code analysis will be performed on a PHP application to exploit an authentication bypass, followed by gaining remote code execution (RCE) through a log poisoning attack. Finally, a misconfigured NFS share will be exploited to obtain root access. This lab focuses on application vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Malbec
description: This lab demonstrates exploiting a remote buffer overflow vulnerability in a custom Windows executable to gain initial access. Learners will escalate privileges by crafting a malicious shared library to exploit a dynamic library hijacking vulnerability in a Linux SUID binary. This lab emphasizes memory corruption exploits, reverse shell payloads, and advanced privilege escalation techniques through library manipulation.

name: Mantis
description: In this lab, an Arbitrary File Read vulnerability will be exploited to obtain MySQL credentials and crack the admin user's hash for web dashboard access, leading to a reverse shell. Privileges will then be escalated using pspy. This lab focuses on file read vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Maria
description: In this lab, we will gain access to the target by exploiting out-of-date WordPress plugins. We will then elevate our privileges by abusing a vulnerable backup solution. This lab focuses on privilege escalation techniques and exploiting outdated software vulnerabilities.

name: Markers
description: In this lab, Learners will leverage enumeration techniques, including web enumeration, to identify system vulnerabilities. They will also exploit markdown-pdf to demonstrate potential security risks. Additionally, the lab covers port forwarding methods and practices privilege escalation to gain higher access levels. This lab focuses on understanding and exploiting security weaknesses in systems.

name: Marketing
description: An authenticated RCE vulnerability in LimeSurvey 5.3.13 will be exploited to gain an initial foothold. Privileges will then be escalated by using mlocate to leak credentials that grant root access. This lab focuses on exploiting application vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Marshalled
description: A monitoring app vulnerable to YAML deserialization will be exploited for initial access. Privileges will then be escalated using a custom binary with a format string vulnerability to obtain a root shell. This lab focuses on exploiting deserialization vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Matrimony
description: In this lab, a DNS reverse lookup will identify the domain name associated with the target's IP address using the dig command. A DNS zone transfer will list all the hosts of the target. The target will be exploited using a publicly available script to log in via SSH. After identifying the Docker interface, a new Docker container will be created and the entire directory mounted. The Docker binary will be imported to check its images. Finally, SSH keys will be added to the root's authorized_keys file to gain a root shell. This lab focuses on DNS enumeration techniques and privilege escalation methods.

name: Matt
description: This lab walks participants through exploiting CVE-2024-47053, an authorization vulnerability in Mautic, to gain administrative access and execute system commands. By leveraging the asset upload feature, attackers obtain a web shell, escalate privileges by cracking a user’s password hash, and ultimately achieve full root access via a misconfigured p7zip sudo permission.

name: MediTrack
description: This lab explores multiple vulnerabilities in the MediTrack web application, starting with an SQL injection in the appointment booking feature. By extracting credentials from the database, an attacker gains access to Gitea, revealing hardcoded secrets and an insecure admin-only deserialization function. This leads to remote code execution (RCE) through a crafted pickle file. Finally, privilege escalation is achieved by exploiting a vulnerable SUID binary to read the root SSH private key, allowing full system compromise.

name: Medjed
description: To compromise this lab, you will exploit an SQL injection vulnerability in a Ruby on Rails web application then escalate your privileges by exploiting insecure folder permissions in the BarracudaDrive v6.5 application, which runs as SYSTEM. This lab will enhance your skills in SQL injection exploitation and privilege escalation through misconfigured application permissions.

name: Megavolt
description: To exploit this lab, you will gain a foothold by stealing an application session cookie and exploiting a client-side vulnerability in osTicket v1.12. After gaining access,  Finally, you will escalate your privileges by leveraging a SUDO misconfiguration, enhancing your understanding of session hijacking, file upload exploitation, and privilege escalation techniques.

name: MiddlewareBypass
description: This lab explores CVE-2025-29927, a vulnerability in Next.js where middleware-based authorization can be bypassed using specially crafted HTTP headers. Learners identify the flaw, exploit it to access protected admin routes, extract sensitive credentials, and gain remote access to the system through SSH.

name: midnight
description: You are required to leverage enumeration techniques, including web enumeration and SMB enumeration, to identify potential vulnerabilities. The lab involves reverse engineering and buffer overflow techniques for binary exploitation. Additionally, Learners will explore privilege escalation through unquoted service paths. This lab focuses on understanding and exploiting vulnerabilities to enhance security awareness.

name: Monster
description: A foothold on the target system will be gained by leveraging a weak password to access the CMS Admin panel. From there, the CMS backup system will be accessed, revealing crackable password hashes that lead to low-privilege access. Privileges will then be elevated to the Administrator account by manipulating writable XAMPP configuration files. This lab focuses on exploiting weak authentication and privilege escalation methods.

name: Muddy
description: In this lab, we'll exploit an XXE (XML External Entity Expansion) vulnerability to access credentials for a WebDAV service. By using WebDAV, we'll upload a reverse shell to establish a foothold on the target. Finally, we'll leverage a cron job PATH to elevate our access to root.

name: MyForum
description: A Chained Remote Command Execution vulnerability in MyBB 1.8.16 will be exploited to gain an initial foothold. Privileges will then be escalated by cracking a hash stored in a MySQL database to obtain root access. This lab focuses on exploiting application vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: MZEEAV
description: In this lab, Learners will employ techniques for enumeration, including web enumeration to identify vulnerabilities. They will explore file upload bypass methods and practice privilege escalation to gain unauthorized access. Finally, the lab covers abusing SUID binaries to exploit privilege flaws. This lab focuses on exploiting security vulnerabilities to understand system weaknesses.

name: Nagoya
description: The lab focuses on exploiting enumeration techniques such as SMB enumeration, Kerberoasting, and MSSQL enumeration. You'll also learn password cracking methods and ticket generation processes. This lab emphasizes practical skills in privilege escalation and credential harvesting.

name: Nappa
description: To exploit this lab, you'll then exploit a commented HTML form code to perform command injection. Finally, you'll decode a base32-encoded password to escalate directly to root, enhancing your skills in identifying and exploiting information disclosure

name: Needle
description: This lab challenges the learner to breach a healthcare-themed web application using a series of advanced web exploitation techniques. It begins with exploiting an XSS vulnerability by uploading a crafted SVG file to a feedback form. Leveraging the stolen session cookies, the attacker bypasses a 403 Forbidden response using custom HTTP headers. The journey continues with uncovering and exploiting an XSLT injection vulnerability, ultimately leading to remote code execution through crafted XSL files. This scenario tests both creativity and precision in navigating and manipulating backend processes.

name: Nibbles
description: Leverage a misconfigured PostgreSQL database server that is listening on all interfaces with default credentials to gain code execution in this lab. Next, exploit misconfigured SUID permissions on the /usr/bin/find binary for privilege escalation. This approach enhances your skills in identifying misconfigurations and escalating privileges effectively.

name: Nickel
description: To exploit this lab, you'll leverage credential disclosure on a web application endpoint to gain an initial foothold. This lab helps you understand how to exploit credential disclosures, crack passwords, and bypass firewall protections for privilege escalation.

name: Nukem
description: To exploit this lab, you'll gain remote code execution (RCE) through a vulnerable plugin in the WordPress installation. This lab teaches you to exploit vulnerabilities in web applications and navigate GUI-based privilege escalation methods.

name: NullByte
description: Apply enumeration and web enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Engage in exploiting SQL Injection vulnerabilities and implement privilege escalation strategies. Additionally, harness the abuse of SUID binaries to enhance your access. This lab is designed to capitalize on your skills in vulnerability exploitation.

name: Ochima
description: The lab focuses on various enumeration techniques, starting with the exploitation of Maltrail to identify vulnerabilities within the target system. Once initial access is achieved, Learners will escalate privileges through strategic methods. Abusing SUID binaries will be a key aspect of privilege escalation to gain higher access levels. This lab teaches the importance of effective enumeration and exploitation techniques in a penetration testing environment.

name: Osaka
description: The lab covers techniques for effective enumeration, including FTP enumeration and buffer overflow attacks. You'll learn how to exploit the SeDebug and SeLoadDriver privileges to gain elevated access. This lab emphasizes the practical application of these skills in privilege escalation scenarios.

name: Outdated
description: An mPDF vulnerability in version 6.0 will be exploited to obtain an initial foothold. Privileges will then be escalated by exploiting a vulnerability in an outdated version of Webmin 1.996. This lab focuses on exploiting application vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Panic
description: In this lab, we'll leverage a buffer overflow vulnerability in a custom web server to compromise this target, allowing us to escalate our privileges by modifying a writable batch script executed by an elevated Scheduled Task.

name: Passport
description: The Passport lab highlights the exploitation of weak credentials, private SSH keys, and misconfigured sudo permissions. Starting with FTP access, learners uncover an SSH private key protected by a passphrase.

name: Pathway
description: This lab explores an arbitrary file read vulnerability in the url-to-png module (CVE-2024-37169), allowing attackers to access sensitive files such as .env, which contains AWS credentials. Using these credentials, an attacker can retrieve user data from an S3 bucket and gain SSH access. Privilege escalation is achieved through LD_PRELOAD shared object hijacking, granting full root control.

name: PayDay
description: In this lab, you will exploit a Local File Inclusion (LFI) vulnerability in an outdated version of CS Cart installed on the PayDay lab. This lab enhances your skills in vulnerability detection, exploitation, and system access techniques.

name: pc
description: This lab emphasizes Nmap enumeration techniques for network scanning and vulnerability assessment. Learners will explore the use of Python pickle for exploitation, gaining insights into the risks associated with deserialization vulnerabilities. The lab provides practical experience in identifying and exploiting weaknesses within a system.

name: Pebbles
description: To compromise this lab, you will exploit an SQL injection vulnerability to gain access to the database. Next, you will leverage a database privilege misconfiguration to launch a root shell. This exercise enhances your skills in exploiting SQL injection and privilege escalation techniques.

name: Pelican
description: To exploit this lab, you'll achieve an initial foothold through an unauthenticated command injection vulnerability. Following that, you'll gain root access by leveraging sudo to disclose a password. This lab enhances your skills in identifying and exploiting command injection vulnerabilities and understanding privilege escalation techniques.

name: Peppo
description: To compromise this lab, we will gain access by exploiting a username exposed via the ident service along with a weak password. We will then escalate our privileges to a root shell by leveraging a vulnerability in a Docker container. This exercise enhances your skills in identifying weak credentials and exploiting container vulnerabilities for privilege escalation.

name: Phobos
description: This lab offers an in-depth exploration of controlling a web application by analyzing its source code. Learners will employ a white-box testing approach to identify and exploit vulnerabilities across three different software platforms. The exercise culminates in escalating access to root privileges by uncovering and cracking a password hash extracted from the local MongoDB database server. Throughout this experience, learners will refine their proficiency in white-box testing, vulnerability assessment, and privilege escalation through password recovery techniques, equipping them with practical skills essential for comprehensive security analysis.

name: Pier
description: In this lab, learners will exploit a known vulnerability, CVE-2024-1651, in TorrentPier 2.4.1. By leveraging insecure deserialization, participants will achieve remote code execution and use it to gain shell access. Through privilege escalation techniques, learners will secure root access on the Ubuntu system. This lab emphasizes enumeration, exploitation, and post-exploitation techniques in a real-world setting.

name: Pipe
description: You are required to leverage enumeration techniques, including web enumeration and WordPress enumeration, to identify potential vulnerabilities. The lab involves password cracking and abusing SUDO permissions for unauthorized access. This lab focuses on understanding and exploiting vulnerabilities to enhance security awareness.

name: PlanetExpress
description: An initial foothold will be gained by exploiting an exposed PHP-FPM FastCGI implementation. Privileges will then be escalated by exploiting a misconfiguration in a SUID binary to read the root password hash, which will be cracked to obtain a root shell. This lab focuses on exploiting web application vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: plum
description: This lab emphasizes different enumeration methods, particularly web enumeration, to uncover vulnerabilities. Learners will exploit CVE-2022-25018 for initial access. The lab also teaches privilege escalation techniques to gain higher-level access within the system.

name: Postfish
description: In this lab, you will exploit the target through phishing for user credentials. You will enumerate potential targets by guessing user credentials for a department mailbox and reading their messages. Following this, you will escalate your privileges by abusing Postfix disclaimer functionality and misconfigured sudo permissions on the /usr/bin/mail binary.

name: Powergrid
description: Employ enumeration and web enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Engage in brute force attacks and utilize methods for exploiting Roundcube. Additionally, implement privilege escalation strategies and harness the abuse of sudo permissions to enhance your access. This lab is designed to capitalize on your skills in vulnerability exploitation.

name: Precision
description: This lab challenges learners to exploit a RISC-V binary with format string and buffer overflow vulnerabilities. After uncovering and analyzing a custom menu-driven service, the attacker leverages a format string bug for an infoleak to bypass ASLR, then overflows the buffer to execute a hidden system("/bin/sh") function, ultimately gaining root access.

name: press
description: This lab involves comprehensive enumeration techniques, including network and web application enumeration, to gather insights about the target system. Learners will exploit CVE-2022-40048 to gain initial access and then focus on privilege escalation methods. By abusing sudo permissions, users will learn effective strategies for gaining elevated access on compromised systems. This lab emphasizes the importance of enumeration and vulnerability exploitation in penetration testing.

name: ProStore
description: A command injection vulnerability will be exploited to establish an initial foothold. Privileges will be escalated by discovering a SUID binary on the lab that is also vulnerable to command injection, leading to root access. This lab focuses on exploiting command injection vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: PwnLab
description: Utilize enumeration and web enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Leverage database enumeration and apply exploitation of the LFI vulnerability. Engage in exploiting file upload vulnerabilities and implement privilege escalation. Additionally, harness path hijacking techniques to enhance your access. This lab is designed to capitalize on your skills in vulnerability exploitation.

name: pyLoader
description: This lab covers essential enumeration techniques, including web enumeration, to identify vulnerabilities in the system. Learners will explore Python Pyloader as a method for exploitation. The lab also focuses on exploiting CVE-2023-0297, demonstrating how to gain initial access to the system.

name: Quackerjack
description: In this lab, you will exploit rConfig to gain remote code execution. You will then elevate your privileges through a dangerous SUID find utility and extend your access using simple C code to launch a reverse shell. This exercise enhances your skills in exploiting vulnerabilities and privilege escalation techniques.

name: Rayeih
description: A thorough enumeration of a GitHub repository will be conducted to discover a set of credentials for initial access. Once on the lab, a vulnerable SUID binary will be located and exploited using a command injection vulnerability to gain root access. This lab focuses on exploiting credential discovery and privilege escalation methods.

name: Readys
description: Utilizing a WordPress plugin LFI vulnerability, access will be gained to a Redis service, which will then be combined with the LFI and Redis access to obtain a foothold on the system. Following this, a cron backup script and wildcard injection will be abused to elevate to root access. This lab focuses on exploiting file inclusion vulnerabilities and privilege escalation techniques.

name: Reconstruction
description: To breach this lab, you'll leverage a local file inclusion vulnerability in a Flask application to enable debug mode. Next, you'll escalate privileges by discovering root user credentials humorously disclosed in a history file. This lab teaches you how to identify local file inclusion vulnerabilities and exploit them for privilege escalation.

name: Resourced
description: Domain controller enumeration will reveal remnants of a password audit that will lead to shell access. Following this, a Resource-Based Constrained Delegation exploitation vector will be leveraged to elevate access to system privileges. This lab focuses on enumeration techniques and privilege escalation methods.

name: Robust
description: Access will be gained by bypassing a 403 Forbidden restriction and the login page using the X-Forwarded-For and Location headers. Finally, we will log in as Administrator via SSH using the discovered credentials. This lab focuses on exploiting web application vulnerabilities and credential enumeration techniques.

name: Rookie Mistake
description: A user's JWT will be modified to gain initial access through a Server-Side Template Injection. Root access will then be obtained by exploiting a command injection vulnerability via the pidstat command. This lab focuses on exploiting template injection vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Roquefort
description: Leverage an authenticated remote code execution vulnerability in Gitea 1.7.5 to gain access in this lab. Then, exploit directory permissions on /usr/local/bin/ to escalate privileges and hijack the PATH search order in cron. This process enhances your skills in vulnerability exploitation and privilege escalation techniques.

name: RPC1
description: An exposed RMI registry will be discovered and enumerated with Remote Method Guesser to detect bindings. Method signatures will be brute-forced to find one that accepts an object, using YsoSerial to test for common gadget chains and gain a foothold. Afterward, a SUID binary for managing the RPC server will be identified, suffering from a BSS-segment-based overflow with a function pointer, allowing for root access. This lab focuses on exploiting remote method invocation vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: RubyDome
description: In this lab, we will perform web enumeration to identify potential attack vectors. We will then exploit discovered vulnerabilities to gain initial access. Privilege escalation will be achieved by abusing sudo permissions, allowing us to gain elevated access on the system. This lab focuses on web enumeration techniques and methods for privilege escalation through misconfigured sudo settings.

name: RussianDolls
description: This lab demonstrates how multiple minor vulnerabilities can be exploited in sequence to achieve full system compromise. Beginning with an SSRF vulnerability, learners will enumerate internal services, exploit path traversal to uncover sensitive files, and extract credentials. The challenge culminates with privilege escalation by abusing a custom binary's functionality to manipulate critical system files. This scenario highlights the cumulative impact of seemingly low-severity flaws.

name: Scarecrow1.1
description: Leverage enumeration and web enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Apply exploitation of the XXE vulnerability and engage in privilege escalation. Additionally, implement process monitoring, use password cracking methods, and harness crontab abuse to enhance your access. This lab is designed to capitalize on your skills in vulnerability exploitation.

name: Scarlet
description: A JWT HS/RSA key confusion vulnerability will be exploited, and a Python script will be created to exploit a SQL injection in the JWT. To escalate privileges, a plaintext attack against ZipCrypto will be employed to obtain root access. This lab focuses on exploiting authentication vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Scrutiny
description: This lab focuses on exploiting TeamCity 2023.05.4 using CVE-2024-27198 for Remote Code Execution (RCE), extracting SSH keys from Git repositories, and leveraging systemctl misconfigurations for privilege escalation.

name: Sea
description: This lab focuses on exploiting a vulnerable SeaCMS installation through both a Local File Inclusion (LFI) and a SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2025-25520). Learners use FTP logs to uncover sensitive paths, retrieve credentials, and gain SSH access. Privilege escalation is achieved by exploiting a cron-executed script and replacing a system binary to trigger a root shell via SUID manipulation.

name: Serialrunning
description: In this lab, you will employ enumeration techniques to identify potential vulnerabilities in Drupal. The lab involves exploiting these vulnerabilities to demonstrate their impact on system security. This lab focuses on understanding and exploiting weaknesses in web applications to enhance security awareness.

name: Shenzi
description: You will discover exposed credentials on an open SMB file share, enabling you to upload a PHP reverse shell to this lab for initial access. Following this, you will exploit an insecure registry configuration to install .msi packages with elevated privileges. This exercise enhances your skills in credential exploitation and privilege escalation through misconfigurations.

name: Shiftdel
description: In this guide, we will gain a foothold by leveraging an arbitrary file deletion vulnerability in WordPress and a local file include in phpMyAdmin. We will then elevate our access by abusing a custom PATH in a cronjob.

name: Shifty
description: To compromise this lab, you will exploit a deserialization vulnerability in a Memcached application. This lab involves achieving privilege escalation by utilizing a hardcoded key from an encryption backup program, enabling you to decrypt encrypted files. This exercise enhances your skills in vulnerability exploitation and privilege escalation techniques.

name: Silicon
description: This scenario involves compromising a vulnerable web app on port 8000 using SQL injection on the case_register_id parameter.

name: Sirol
description: To compromise this lab, you will exploit the Timelion visualizer in the Kibana app to gain a foothold. Upon discovery that the target is Dockerized, you will escape the container by mounting the GlusterFS filesystem and setting up a cron job to establish a privileged shell. Additionally, you will explore an alternate escape method by chrooting the mounted filesystem. This exercise enhances your skills in container exploitation and privilege escalation techniques.

name: SkillForge
description: Explore a multi-layered environment beginning with a misconfigured FTP server and culminating in full system compromise via container escape and privilege escalation. Uncover sensitive credentials, exploit an RCE in pgAdmin, pivot through a Docker container using Ligolo-ng, and ultimately leverage CVE-2024-12905—a vulnerability in the tar-fs Node.js module—to overwrite an SSH key and achieve root access.

name: Slort
description: In this lab, you will exploit a remote file inclusion vulnerability in a web application. You will then escalate privileges by leveraging misconfigured permissions on an executable that operates under the system job scheduler. This exercise enhances your skills in vulnerability exploitation and privilege escalation techniques.

name: Snookums
description: To compromise this lab, you will exploit an RFI vulnerability in the Simple PHP Photo Gallery web application to gain access to a low-level user account. This exercise enhances your skills in vulnerability exploitation and privilege escalation techniques.

name: Sona
description: In this lab, we'll leverage a question-answer guessing technique in Nexus Backup Manager to compromise this target by exposing a password for the Nexus Repository Manager Java EL Injection CVE. We'll then employ a Python Library Hijacking attack to escalate our privileges, taking advantage of open permissions on a script that runs as root every minute.

name: Sorcerer
description: To exploit this lab, you'll leverage various web server leaks to gain an initial foothold. This lab teaches you about information gathering through web server leaks, exploiting user scripts for shell access, and understanding SUID misconfigurations for privilege escalation.

name: Source
description: The password reset function will be leveraged to enumerate valid email accounts and bypass login lockout limits to obtain a set of credentials. An arbitrary file upload vulnerability in eLabFTW 1.8.5 will be exploited to establish an initial foothold. Privileges will then be escalated by thoroughly enumerating a .git repository and overwriting an insecure HTTP smoke testing script to gain root access. This lab focuses on exploiting account enumeration and privilege escalation methods.

name: Spaghetti
description: In this scenario, we'll leverage a vulnerable IRC bot to compromise the target system. We'll then escalate our access by injecting commands into a table on the local MySQL server and exploiting a cron job to execute them.

name: SpiderSociety
description: This lab challenges learners to uncover and exploit misconfigurations within a seemingly secure network environment. By identifying exposed internal services and leveraging weak credentials, learners gain initial access before pivoting through the system to escalate privileges. The scenario emphasizes enumeration, abuse of common tools, and lateral movement, testing real-world penetration skills in a layered, realistic setup.

name: Splodge
description: To compromise this lab, you will gain a foothold by leveraging Git repository files containing valid credentials. You'll then escalate privileges by exploiting insecure ownership of the PostgreSQL database process and abusing a sudo misconfiguration, enhancing your ability to exploit database misconfigurations and privilege escalation tactics.

name: SpringAuth_attack
description: Gain a foothold through an exposed WordPress site and misconfigured FTP server, then pivot to exploit a Spring Boot application vulnerable to CVE-2024-38821. This path traversal flaw allows access to sensitive configuration files revealing SSH credentials. After initial access, escalate privileges by hijacking a writable cron script to gain root access.

name: SPX
description: Approaches for identifying potential vulnerabilities are utilized in this lab. The focus is on exploiting CVE-2024-42007, practicing privilege escalation, and abusing SUDO permissions for unauthorized access. This lab emphasizes understanding and exploiting vulnerabilities to enhance security awareness.

name: Squid
description: In this lab, we will enumerate ports behind a Squid proxy to gain an initial foothold through phpMyAdmin. Privileges will then be elevated by creating scheduled tasks to enable restricted privileges. This lab focuses on exploiting proxy configurations and privilege escalation methods.

name: sshcontrol
description: This lab explores a web application running on Node.js vulnerable to time-based SQL injection, allowing extraction of user credentials and password hashes. The challenge deepens with a character-by-character brute force attack on a master password validation endpoint, enabling SSH key injection and local access. From there, privilege escalation is achieved through a vulnerable root cronjob script executing unsanitized input via eval, ultimately leading to full system compromise. The scenario emphasizes stealthy enumeration, web app exploitation, and command injection through poorly validated configurations.

name: SugarVale
description: SugarVale demonstrates a full-stack web-to-root attack starting with leaked secrets in .env, used to forge a valid admin JWT. The admin interface contains a server-side template injection (SSTI) that enables remote code execution. Attackers escalate privileges by appending a SUID shell payload to a group-writable script run by root via cron, achieving full root compromise.

name: SunsetTwilight
description: Employ enumeration and web enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Engage in exploiting LFI vulnerabilities and utilize methods for bypassing file uploads. Additionally, implement SMB enumeration and apply privilege escalation strategies to enhance your access. This lab is designed to capitalize on your skills in vulnerability exploitation.

name: Surf
description: Using a cookie-based authentication bypass along with a blind Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) exploit, we will gain access to the target system. Afterward, another account will be compromised to abuse sudo permissions for privilege escalation. This lab focuses on exploiting authentication vulnerabilities and privilege escalation techniques.

name: Sybaris
description: To compromise this lab, you'll gain remote code execution by utilizing the Redis MODULE LOAD command alongside an anonymous FTP service to upload a malicious module. Subsequently, you'll exploit a root-run cron job by leveraging a malicious shared object file in a writable directory within the cron LD_LIBRARY_PATH.

name: Symbolic
description: In this lab, a Local File Inclusion vulnerability in a web server will be exploited. Access will then be elevated by leveraging an automated backup task and Windows symbolic links. This lab focuses on exploiting web application vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Synapse
description: In this lab, we will exploit a Server Side Includes (SSI) injection vulnerability in a web application, which allows us to crack a GPG-encrypted text file containing user credentials for SSH access. We will leverage a Python script running with elevated privileges to perform a socket command injection attack, granting us arbitrary command execution as root.

name: Ted
description: Leverage enumeration and web enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Utilize brute force attacks and engage in privilege escalation. Additionally, harness sudo permission abuse to enhance your access. This lab is designed to capitalize on your skills in vulnerability exploitation.

name: Thor
description: Access to the lab will be gained by exploiting a command injection vulnerability in OpenLiteSpeed WebServer. Privileges will then be escalated by using Metasploit to exploit a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in a vulnerable Webmin service. This lab focuses on exploiting command injection and privilege escalation methods.

name: Tico
description: In this lab, you will exploit the target by obtaining and cracking a MongoDB authentication handshake exchange found within a PCAP file on an anonymous FTP server. After acquiring the MongoDB admin user's password, you will exploit a vulnerable NodeBB plugin, enabling you to write arbitrary files to the file system. This NodeBB application runs with the highest privileges, allowing the exploit to overwrite the root user's authorized_keys file, granting you SSH access.

name: Tux
description: This lab explores a multi-stage exploitation chain starting from a file upload bypass via double extensions in Apache, leading to remote code execution. Learners will pivot into an isolated Docker container, bypass command filters for shell access, and exploit a world-writable script for credential extraction. The final stage involves abusing a custom SUID archiving tool vulnerable to wildcard injection to gain root privileges. Skills tested include web application exploitation, container breakout, pivoting, privilege escalation, and binary analysis.

name: Twiggy
description: In this lab, we will gain access by exploiting a pre-auth remote code execution vulnerability on a SaltStack master. This will allow us to execute commands on the master by creating a runner of salt.cmd using the cmd.exec_code function. This exercise enhances your skills in exploiting vulnerabilities for command execution and system access.

name: UC404
description: To exploit this lab, you'll leverage OS command injection in a web application to gain an initial foothold and then employ a password disclosure along with a sudo misconfiguration to escalate your privileges, enhancing your skills in exploiting command injection vulnerabilities and understanding privilege escalation techniques through misconfigurations.

name: Upsploit
description: Source code analysis will reveal an arbitrary file upload vulnerability, allowing the upload of a JSP webshell for initial access. Privileges will then be escalated by abusing a cron job running a custom binary that suffers from command injection. This lab focuses on exploiting file upload vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: USV2017
description: Engage in enumeration and web enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Utilize de-obfuscating JavaScript code methods and leverage the exploitation of LFI vulnerabilities. Apply password cracking techniques and harness SQL injection exploitation to enhance your skills. This lab is designed to capitalize on your abilities in vulnerability exploitation.

name: Validator
description: An Expression Language (EL) injection found in a public repository will be exploited to establish an initial foothold. Privileges will be escalated by exploiting a SUID binary with a malicious RubyGems library to gain root access. This lab focuses on exploiting EL injection vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Vanity
description: A command injection vulnerability will be exploited to obtain an initial foothold. Privileges will then be escalated by taking advantage of a wildcard injection in a cron job to gain root access. This lab focuses on exploiting command injection vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Vault
description: A foothold on the target will be gained by using a writable SMB share to execute a URI file attack. Following this, SYSTEM privilege will be elevated by abusing write access on a Group Policy Object. This lab focuses on exploiting SMB vulnerabilities and privilege escalation techniques.

name: Vector
description: To breach this lab, you will perform a padding oracle attack against a web application using an unauthenticated AES-CBC encryption scheme. This lab focuses on exploiting cryptographic vulnerabilities and password recovery techniques.

name: Virus
description: A network service hosting a custom binary challenge built for a non-native CPU architecture, centered on reverse engineering, anti-debugging bypass, and constraint-based input solving.

name: vmdak
description: Methods for uncovering potential vulnerabilities are employed in this lab. It focuses on web enumeration, web exploitation, and MySQL enumeration, along with practicing privilege escalation for unauthorized access. This lab emphasizes understanding and exploiting vulnerabilities to enhance security awareness.

name: VoIP
description: In this lab, we'll leverage weak web application credentials to compromise this target by exploiting a SIP digest leak vulnerability in a VoIP server. We'll then employ this access to retrieve and decode a raw RTP stream containing the SSH password for a local user, whose username is also leaked from the web app. With unrestricted sudo permissions, we will gain root access.

name: Walla
description: To gain control of this lab, you will exploit the enabled web console in a RaspAP web application by using default authentication credentials. You will then escalate privileges by exploiting the Python module import order in a script that can be executed with sudo privileges. This lab will enhance your understanding of web application vulnerabilities and privilege escalation techniques in Python.

name: WallpaperHub
description: This lab demonstrates the exploitation of an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in a wallpaper sharing platform. Learners will perform local file inclusion to extract sensitive files, retrieve a database with hashed credentials, and crack them for SSH access. Privilege escalation is achieved by exploiting a vulnerable happy-dom package (CVE-2024-51757) in a web scraping tool, ultimately gaining root access through a crafted HTML payload.

name: Wheels
description: In this lab, an XPATH injection will be used to gain an initial foothold, followed by reverse-engineering a binary to read the contents of /etc/shadow and crack the root hash for root access. This lab focuses on exploiting injection vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.

name: Wombo
description: Leverage a remote code execution vulnerability in a Redis data store to gain root access in this lab. This exercise enhances your skills in identifying and exploiting vulnerabilities for privilege escalation.

name: workaholic
description: This lab explores an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the WP-Advanced-Search plugin (CVE-2024-9796). By exploiting this flaw, an attacker can enumerate WordPress users, extract password hashes, and crack them to gain FTP access. Further, the attacker retrieves database credentials from wp-config.php, leading to SSH access. Privilege escalation is achieved via an SUID binary vulnerable to shared object injection, granting full root control.

name: XposedAPI
description: In this lab, you will exploit an API functionality in a web application then escalate your privileges by taking advantage of misconfigured SUID permissions on the wget binary. This lab will enhance your understanding of API exploitation and privilege escalation through SUID misconfigurations.

name: Y0usef
description: Utilize enumeration and web enumeration techniques to identify vulnerabilities. Engage in exploiting host header vulnerabilities and file upload vulnerabilities, alongside implementing privilege escalation strategies. This lab is designed to capitalize on your skills in vulnerability exploitation.

name: Zab
description:
## Summary

This lab challenges you to exploit misconfigurations in Mage AI and Zabbix to escalate privileges to root. Gaining initial access through Mage AI, you'll extract database credentials and leverage port forwarding to access the restricted Zabbix UI. By abusing Zabbix’s script execution feature, you'll execute arbitrary commands, elevate privileges to zabbix, and ultimately escalate to root using rsync misconfigurations.

name: ZenPhoto
description: Employ a remote code execution vulnerability in the Zenphoto web application to compromise the target in this lab. After gaining access, escalate privileges through a local kernel exploit, enhancing your skills in vulnerability detection and system access techniques.

name: Zino
description: In this lab, we will exploit the Booked Scheduler web application using credentials obtained from an open Samba share. We will then upload a PHP reverse shell for initial access. Following that, we will escalate privileges by modifying a scheduled script to execute a reverse shell, ultimately gaining root access. This exercise enhances your skills in exploiting web applications and privilege escalation techniques.

name: Zipper
description: A file upload capability and Local File Inclusion (LFI) will be chained to upload a malicious zip file and gain an initial foothold. Privileges will then be escalated by discovering a cron job that includes a *.zip wildcard, which is vulnerable to an arbitrary error that allows reading a file to obtain root access. This lab focuses on exploiting file upload vulnerabilities and privilege escalation methods.
